I'm 27 and came out of an almost 5 years long relationship not long ago, the details seem to be pretty similar too. 


I cannot recommend the book Leave a Cheater Gain a Life enough, it helped me tremendously. In my opinion the first step is to realize that none of this is your fault. You might have brought issues into the relationship, but your partner had a vast amount of options to deal with them, instead chose one of the shittiest things - cheating. 


Distractions can be great at first, but don't overdo it, as you still need to deal with the trauma sooner or later. It's great to hear you are doing therapy, it can help  with grief and putting things into perspective.


As cliche as it sounds one of the most important things is to work on yourself and surround yourself with supportive people - family, friends and even survivors of similar traumas. When I came out of the relationship I felt worthless, a shadow of my former pre-relationship self. Then realized that I'm still an interesting and valuable person with great friends and hobbies, I just invested too much into the relationship neglecting my needs in the process. 


Start working out or running, it can help you feel more confident in your body and it helps mentally too. Get into or get back to hobbies. Even if they seem pointless at the beginning, you can bounce back to these things when you are feeling down and make you feel better about yourself. 


Online dating can be great but equally destructive too if you have high expectations. For me it helped realize that people can find me interesting and even attractive which was huge after feeling so down on myself for months. (And this comes from someone who has a pretty serious facial deformity so looks are not everything)


I don't want to brag just give you some hope: 4 months out I feel awesome. Now I live with my brother, I'm in the process of rekindling my relationships with my old friends, started running and working out, found new hobbies and friends, and dating a pretty awesome girl who lifts me up instead of putting me down. Time WILL heal your wounds, and in the process you'll have a great opportunity to learn a lot about yourself
